choice: Dissociative Haber–Bosch surface mechanism: N2 adsorption/dissociation to N*, sequential hydrogenation N*→NH*→NH2*→NH3*, and NH3 desorption; allow hydride/electride supports to change the rate-controlling step but retain the same overall stoichiometry.
alternatives: Associative distal/alternating N2 hydrogenation as the universal mechanism
Pure empirical conversion interpolation without elementary interpretation
reason: The conventional Fe/Ru literature and electride-supported Ru paper support dissociative activation, while hydride promotion can shift the bottleneck; chemical-looping papers were excluded, so a lattice-nitrogen mechanism is outside the modeled boundary.

choice: Map each reported productivity to plant conditions with a reversible approach-to-equilibrium rate: forward activity scaled by Arrhenius temperature and empirical N2/H2 pressure orders, multiplied by max(0,1-Q/Kp); calibrate the catalyst-specific prefactor to each laboratory record and optimize per-pass conversion below equilibrium.
alternatives: Use laboratory conversion directly at plant conditions
Single universal Temkin–Pyzhev prefactor for all catalysts
Assume every catalyst reaches equilibrium regardless of activity
reason: Record-specific calibration preserves measured activity while the reversible driving-force term prevents impossible conversion; pressure/composition scaling and catalyst inventory expose the economic tradeoff between activity, recycle, equilibrium, and catalyst cost.

choice: High-pressure multibed adiabatic fixed-bed ammonia converter represented by one equilibrium-limited reactor block with externalized heat removal/recovery and optimized loop pressure, temperature, and per-pass conversion.
reason: Industrial ammonia synthesis uses robust packed catalyst beds; the aggregate block permits literature catalysts to be compared while preserving equilibrium, catalyst inventory, reaction heat, and recycle tradeoffs.

choice: Cool and condense ammonia at loop pressure, separate liquid NH3 in a knockout, purge a small gas fraction, and recycle H2/N2.
alternatives: Cryogenic distillation of the full loop gas
reason: Condensation plus recycle is the conventional high-pressure synthesis-loop architecture and directly couples separation and recycle duty to per-pass conversion; absorption is retained only as an excluded alternative because the catalyst corpus is not uniformly measured with sorbents.

choice: Purchased purified H2 and N2 at 30 bar through synthesis, recycle, condensation, and pressurized liquid NH3 handling; upstream feed manufacture and downstream distribution excluded.
alternatives: Include natural-gas reforming and air separation
Include ammonia shipping and end use
reason: This boundary isolates whether catalyst laboratory ranking predicts synthesis-plant choice while still capturing all catalyst-dependent equipment, energy, equilibrium, recycle, and separation effects.

choice: Use nitrogen adsorption energy ΔE_N (eV per N atom relative to 1/2 N2 and a vacant site) as the descriptor in a dissociative N2/H2 microkinetic model; weaker binding limits N2 activation, stronger binding penalizes N hydrogenation, producing a Sabatier volcano.
alternatives: NHx adsorption energy as an independent descriptor
Empirical metal identity without atom-scale kinetics
reason: Nitrogen binding is the canonical ammonia-synthesis descriptor connecting N2 dissociation and removal of strongly bound N-derived intermediates; linear scaling and BEP relations permit a thermodynamically closed model and backward design.
